_comment: Hook commands are anchored to ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} (the repo root), NOT repo-relative. A bare relative path (hooks/x.sh, shipped 1.22.2-1.23.2) only resolves while the spawning shell's cwd IS the repo root — Claude Code spawns each hook command with cwd = wherever the session currently is, which drifts the moment the agent runs `cd`. Proven live on CLI 2.1.220: a PreToolUse:Bash hook wired with a bare relative path fired once from root, then silently never fired again after a single `cd sub/deep` inside the same session — every following tool call ran ungated, no error, no log line. ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} is a real env var Claude Code sets on every hook process (docs: code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md), pinned to the repo root regardless of later cd's; anchoring with it kept the identical hook firing both before and after the same cd. ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} still does not resolve here — different variable, same non-resolution PR #29 already found. NOT fixed by this: a session LAUNCHED with cwd already inside a subdirectory never discovers this file at all (six independent live trials, CLI 2.1.220, both 1- and 2-level-deep launches, plain and ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}-anchored commands alike) — unlike .claude/settings.local.json, which the docs state explicitly resolves through the repo root, .claude/settings.json is not documented to walk up, and empirically does not. No hook fires for that session's entire lifetime, and no command-path anchoring can fix a file that is never read. Tracked as BACKLOG A23 — launch from the repo root until that's closed. EVERY command below is additionally wrapped in a literal pair of double quotes around the FULL expanded path (embedded via JSON's \" escape, so bash sees "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/hooks/x.sh" as one word) — anchoring alone was not sufficient, per a reviewer on this same PR: an unquoted ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} expansion word-splits on whitespace, and CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR is a real filesystem path that can legitimately contain a space. Proven live: bash -c on the unquoted anchored form with a spaced CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR exits 127 (command not found, path split at the space) instead of running the hook — and per Claude Code's own exit-code contract (code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md), exit 127 is a NON-BLOCKING error for both PreToolUse and Stop, so the tool call proceeds exactly as if no hook were configured. This is fail-open: a force-push command that guard.sh correctly blocks (exit 2, C-02) when the path resolves produces no BLOCKED message and exit 127 instead the instant the path is unquoted and spaced — the guard never starts, so it never gets a chance to deny. Full evidence and the red/green reproduction: docs/BACKLOG.md A23; regression guard: tests/hooks_test.sh's spaced-project-dir fixture.
